title: Exploratory testing charters
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for exploratory testing in time-boxed sessions: charters with one mission each, notes taken as the session happens, every bug proposed as a finding, a debrief by a different worker and coverage notes that say what was and was not explored.
boundaries: One charter per session, inside its time box; an overrun is recorded with the reason.
Sessions are read-only on live targets; booking, submitting or creating runs only on a test target a person named.
Notes, bugs and coverage stay on the record; a later session never rewrites an earlier one.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for exploratory testing in time-boxed sessions

value.lets_workers: Draft time-boxed charters from risks, recent findings or test results; explore one charter per session and take timestamped notes as it happens; turn every bug into a proposed finding and every question into an issue; have a different worker debrief the session; and keep coverage notes that say what was explored and what was not.

flow.when: When a release, a change or a set of findings needs exploring.
One charter per session, within its time box, by an agent or a person.
Right after the session, by a different worker or a person.
After several sessions, or before deciding to stop exploring.

guardrails: One mission per charter and one charter per session, inside a time box; running over is recorded with the reason.
Notes are taken while exploring, with times; a session written up afterwards from memory fails the session checks.
Every bug becomes a proposed finding with evidence; every open question is recorded as an issue.
Coverage notes always say what was not explored. Exploring is never called complete.
Sessions are read-only on live targets; anything that would book, buy or create an account needs a test target a person named.
complements: Scripted acceptance runs go through the user acceptance testing pack; exploration finds what no script asked about.
Bugs go to the findings to fixes pack; accessibility problems are confirmed with the accessibility audit pack.

nouns.title: How exploratory testing runs in charters, sessions and debriefs
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: draft-charters writes missions from risks, findings, acceptance results or audit reports.
run-session explores one charter within its time box and keeps timestamped notes.
debrief-session: a different worker or a person asks the debrief questions and confirms the bugs.
map-coverage combines sessions into coverage notes and proposes charters for the gaps.
rules: Exploration is learning, test design and test execution at the same time; the charter guides it without scripting it.
A session that drifts off its mission records the drift as a note and a proposed new charter.
Bugs are problems that threaten the product's value; issues are questions or obstacles that need someone's answer.
Failures stay on the record; a later session never rewrites an earlier one's notes.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

debrief_questions.feelings: How does the tester feel about the product's quality here?

sources: Session-based test management, described by Jonathan Bach in 2000: charters, time-boxed sessions, session sheets and debriefs.
The charter form explore a target, with resources, to discover information, popularized by Elisabeth Hendrickson's book Explore It! (2013).
Product elements and quality criteria as test-idea prompts, after James Bach's Heuristic Test Strategy Model.
The wording, rules and examples here are written for this pack.

nouns.title: How to write an exploratory testing charter
nouns.category_reason: A reusable method for writing charters.

value.form: Explore a target, with resources, to discover information. For example: explore the sign-up form with only a keyboard to discover where focus gets lost.
rules: One mission per charter, small enough for one time box.
Name the risks the charter is aimed at and why it matters now, such as a recent fix or a failed acceptance step.
List resources: personas, devices, settings, data and tools, all made-up or public.
Say what is out of scope, so a session that drifts can tell.

nouns.title: Prompts for test ideas during a session
nouns.category_reason: A reusable set of prompts; using them takes judgment.

product_elements.structure: What it is made of: pages, files, components.
product_elements.function: What it does, including error handling.
product_elements.data: What it takes in and gives out: empty, long, odd characters, other languages.
product_elements.interfaces: How people and other systems reach it: forms, links, APIs, keyboard.
product_elements.platform: What it depends on: browsers, screen sizes, themes, networks.
product_elements.operations: How it is really used: interruptions, back and forward, many tabs.
product_elements.time: What changes over time: timeouts, dates, slow responses, stale pages.

tours.name: keyboard-only tour
tours.try: Do every task with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and Escape only.

tours.name: small-screen tour
tours.try: Do every task at 320 and 390 pixels wide, in both orientations.

tours.name: error tour
tours.try: Make every mistake a hurried person would, on a test target, and read every message.

tours.name: back-button tour
tours.try: Go back, forward and reload at every step and see what is kept.

tours.name: slow-network tour
tours.try: Throttle the connection and watch for missing progress or double actions.

tours.name: words tour
tours.try: Read every label and message as a newcomer would; note jargon and claims that need checking.

nouns.title: Rules every exploratory session follows
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule set for sessions.

value.time_box: Stop at the time box. Up to ten minutes over is allowed to finish a reproduction; record overran and why.
value.notes: At least one timestamped note every fifteen minutes, written as it happens.
value.split: Record the share of time spent on setup, on testing and on investigating and reporting bugs, in whole percents adding to 100.
value.bugs: Every bug has steps a different worker can follow and evidence stored by SHA-256, and becomes a proposed record-finding verb.
value.issues: Every question or obstacle is written as a question someone can answer.
value.coverage: Say what was covered and what was not; never write that everything was covered.
value.data: Made-up or public data only. On a live target, never book, buy, submit or create an account; that needs a test target a person named.

nouns.title: Deriving coverage from sessions
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same sessions always give the same coverage.

value.grid: Rows are areas of the product; columns are the quality criteria in the test ideas.

statuses.explored: At least one debriefed session covered it with its charter done.
statuses.partly: A session touched it, but the debrief says continue or it was noted as not covered.
statuses.out_of_scope: A person ruled it out, with the reason.

value.gaps: Every row that is not_explored or partly is a gap; each gap gets a proposed charter.
value.never: A coverage note never says complete; it says what is known as of its date.

nouns.title: Record checks for session notes, with made-up golden notes
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic checks with made-up known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes them.

value.purpose: Checks every exploratory session's notes must pass before its debrief: the exact charter and build, a time box, notes taken during the session, bugs with evidence, questions and honest coverage. The two made-up good sessions pass; each made-up bad one fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: The notes pin the exact charter.
The notes repeat the charter's mission.
The notes say whether an agent or a person explored.
The session had a time box.
A session that ran over says why.
Notes were taken during the session, not only at the end.
Every note has a time, a kind and text.
Every bug has steps and evidence stored by digest.
Every issue is a question someone can answer.
The notes say what was covered.
The notes say what was not covered.
Notes hold no email addresses or phone numbers.

verbs.title: Draft exploratory charters
verbs.summary: Write one to eight time-boxed charters, each with one mission in the explore, with, to discover form, its resources, the risks it targets and why it matters now.

slots.name: target_brief
slots.description: Pin of a brief naming the target, its build and what changed.

slots.name: risk_sources
slots.description: Pins of findings, acceptance results or audit reports to aim at, if any.

steps: Start from the pinned risk sources: open findings, failed or blocked acceptance steps, audit cannot_tell results and recent changes.
Write one mission per charter in the charter form, small enough for its time box.
List made-up or public resources, the risks targeted, test ideas from the prompts and what is out of scope.
Rank the charters by risk and say why each matters now.

acceptance.check: Every charter validates against template.charter's schema.
Every mission follows the charter form and names one target.
time_box_minutes is 45, 90 or 120 to match time_box.
Each charter is aimed at a risk the sources support.

verbs.title: Run one exploratory session
verbs.summary: Explore one charter within its time box, taking timestamped notes as you go, recording every bug with steps and evidence and every question as an issue.
verbs.outcome: Session notes, with a finding proposed for every bug.

slots.name: charter
slots.description: Pin of the charter to explore.

test_target_named.description: True only when a person named a test target for actions that book, submit or create.

steps: Confirm the charter and the build before starting; if the build differs from the charter's, end blocked.
Explore within the charter's mission and resources, and write a timestamped note at least every fifteen minutes as it happens.
Record each bug with steps a different worker can follow and evidence by SHA-256, and each open question as an issue.
Stop at the time box; record overran and why if you finish a reproduction.
Never book, buy, submit or create an account on a live target unless test_target_named is true, and use only made-up data.
Propose findings-to-fixes.record-finding for every bug and a new charter for any drift.

acceptance.check: The notes validate against template.session-notes's schema.
The notes pass every pinned session check.
setup_pct, test_pct and bug_pct add up to 100.
The output proposes one record-finding verb per bug.

network: Read-only page loads and keyboard navigation on the charter's target; anything that would book, submit or create runs only on a test target a person named.

verbs.title: Debrief the session
verbs.summary: A worker who did not run the session asks the debrief questions, confirms or questions each bug and decides whether the charter is done, continues or is abandoned.
verbs.outcome: A debrief with new charters for what the session left open.
steps: Confirm you did not run the session; otherwise end blocked.
Answer the five debrief questions from the notes and, when the tester is a person, with them.
Confirm or question every bug from its steps and evidence, and write a new charter for each gap worth exploring.

acceptance.check: The debrief validates against template.debrief's schema.
Every bug in the notes is confirmed or questioned.

verbs.title: Map what has been explored
verbs.summary: Combine sessions and debriefs into coverage notes by area and quality criterion, list every gap and propose a charter for each.
verbs.outcome: Coverage notes that never call exploring complete.
steps: Give every area and quality criterion a status by the coverage model, citing the sessions.
List every gap and propose a charter for each in the charter form.
Count open bugs from the debriefs, and never describe the coverage as complete.

acceptance.check: The coverage notes validate against template.coverage-notes's schema.
Recomputing the statuses from the pinned sessions and debriefs gives the same values.
Every gap has a proposed charter.
